strengthening.reason: Every incidence degree d_x is an integer and sum_x d_x=L, hence min_x d_x <= floor(L/n).

base_theorem.name: BOUNDED_WIDTH_LOW_INCIDENCE_PIVOT_IS_RAW_CAP_SAFE
base_theorem.statement: For canonical F of state size s<=C and maximum clause width w>=2, any live pivot x of incidence degree d_x<=D_w(Delta) is raw-cap safe, with pure pivots safe directly and D_w(Delta)=2*((w+1)+sqrt((w+1)^2+(2w-1)*Delta))/(2w-1), Delta=C-s.

integer_corollary.name: INTEGER_AVERAGE_DEGREE_FORCES_SAFE_PIVOT
integer_corollary.statement: Since all d_x are nonnegative integers and sum_x d_x=L, at least one live variable satisfies d_x<=floor(L/n). Therefore floor(L/n)<=D_w(Delta) guarantees an ordinary exact capped pivot.
proof: If every d_x were at least floor(L/n)+1, their sum would be at least n*(floor(L/n)+1)>L, contradiction.
Choose x with d_x<=floor(L/n). If floor(L/n)<=D_w(Delta), then d_x<=D_w(Delta).
Apply the proved bounded-width low-incidence pivot theorem.
integer_corollary.contrapositive_pressure: If every live pivot truly overflows, then every integer degree d_x >= floor(D_w(Delta))+1, hence L >= n*(floor(D_w(Delta))+1).

frozen_ladder_theorem.statement: Every canonical width-3 state in each frozen parameter rung that has exactly the listed n live variables and clause count has at least one ordinary raw-cap-safe pivot under the rung's N^2 cap. Therefore none of the four frozen rungs can reach the all_pivot_overflow filter, independently of finite enumeration order or the 12000-state limit.
frozen_ladder_theorem.relationship_to_ci: Workflow run 33076460274 observed zero all-pivot-overflow states in its bounded samples, consistent with but not needed for this theorem.

new_frontier: The old width-3 local-gap ladder is no longer an informative v3 stressor. Future adversaries must choose parameters/widths satisfying the necessary integer pressure L >= n*(floor(D_w(Delta))+1), while still respecting the original-N cap and earlier exact-lane filters.
